messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Problem with Correlations in Ordinal SEM
parts:
I am not sure it is estimated or the parameter is fixed as 0 in one model and free in the other model. In your script, I would try to put the following line:

y1 ~~ NA*y2

Then, the covariance between y1 and y2 should not be exactly equal to 0.

Sunthud

On Thu, Nov 6, 2014 at 1:46 PM, Deuterium <mahers...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,

Attached is the SEM I'm currently using in my research. When estimating the model in lavaan, the covariance between y1 and y2 is being estimated as 0.000. However, in previous iterations of the model where I was estimating y1 and y2 as continuous (all else the same), the covariance was being estimated as 0.45 by lavaan. Also, calculating the polychoric covariance of y1 and y2 on the side yields 0.44.

What could this problem be due to? And is there something I should do in order to enable lavaan to estimate the covariance in the attached model?

Also, I wonder how cov(y1,y2) enters the formulation of the SEM. I mean, is cov(y1,y2) included somehow in the implied covariance matrix which is used for estimation? (my reference on SEM is Bollen (1989) and I haven't ran into a case with a covariance similar to mine).

Thank you,
Deuterium

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Problem with Correlations in Ordinal SEM
parts: It would be helpful if I see your syntax and lavaan command. Another thing is that if you would like to estimate residual covariances of y1 and y2 when both y1 and y2 are categorical, you need to use theta parameterization. That is, in the cfa function, you need to specify parameterization = "theta".
